results.title: Digital levers for sustainability: a meta-analytic review of ...
results.content: Some studies report strong positive links between DT and ESG, especially when digital investment fuels green innovation, supports evidence-based decisions, or enhances disclosure quality (Ding et al., Citation2024; Wu, Citation2024). To clarify these effects, DT is categorized into five typologies: (i) General DT maturity (e.g. digital orientation, IT investment intensity) (Pham et al., Citation2024), (ii) AI and intelligent systems (e.g. predictive analytics, robotics) (Al Halbusi et al., Citation2025), (iii) Data and Infrastructure (e.g. big data platforms, cloud systems), (iv) Business Process Digitization (e.g. ERP, workflow automation) (Wang & Zhang, Citation2024), and (v) Innovation Capabilities (e.g. smart product development, digital R&D) (Khan et al., Citation2023). Dynamic-Capabilities research shows that sectors built around rapid innovation, e.g. ICT and platform services, reconfigure digital tools faster than heavy manufacturing or multi-sector conglomerates, magnifying DT’s ESG impact (Kong et al., Citation2024; Luo, Citation2024). These results reinforce Fu and Li (Citation2023) moderation findings: AI improves ESG performance only in firms with high digital maturity and strong internal controls.

results.title: Reproducible research policies and software/data ...
results.content: # Reproducible research policies and software/data management in scientific computing journals: a survey, discussion, and perspectives Best practices in data management are covered in Section 3.6, and Section 3.7 discusses the role of scientific publishers in reproducible research, including new types of publications with code and the challenges of evaluating research artifacts. In Section 4, a survey of 16 computer science journals provides insights into experiences implementing data-code sharing policies based on the reviewed reproducibility platforms and technologies. One difficulty is to measure (Rosenblatt et al., 2023) the degrees of reproducibility depending on the complexity, type of reproducibility, type of data (Ahmed et al., 2022), and field of the research study (Raff, 2020) given that despite what is generally expected from computer systems and as has been shown in multiple positions (Gundersen and Kjensmo, 2018; Raghupathi et al., 2022; Bailey, 2020; Jalal Apostal et al., 2020), executing the same code on a different machine does not generate the same numerical result, but it can be established that a result is statistically similar (Raff, 2019). Citation: Hernandez JA and Colom M (2025) Reproducible research policies and software/data management in scientific computing journals: a survey, discussion, and perspectives.
